findings.claim: The plan has the skill write docs pages, create Diataxis folders and edit docs/README.md itself, but the manifesto says 'Skills route; kmctl decides and writes', and scaffold-init says Diataxis folders 'are created by the verbs that add their first page'. No ticket adds such a verb: new-concept-verbs covers only .okf concepts. So either this ticket must add a `kmctl new doc TYPE TITLE` verb (page, folder, index entry), or the plan must say the docs skill is an exception. That choice changes the scope and what the skill calls.

The skill edits docs/README.md, which only exists after `kmctl init` (scaffold-init), and its index entries must match what `kmctl check` (knowledge-check) treats as listed. depends_on names only claude-plugin, so the skill could be built against an index format that scaffold-init and knowledge-check then define differently, and the done test (four requests landing in the right folders) has no defined repository to run in. Add scaffold-init (and the verb from p1, if chosen) to depends_on, or say the skill creates docs/README.md when it is missing.

The skill no longer writes docs structure itself: it creates pages with `kmctl new doc TYPE TITLE` from the new ticket new-doc-verb (folder, skeleton, index entry) and writes only the prose, as the manifesto's 'skills route; kmctl writes' requires.

depends_on now names claude-plugin, new-doc-verb and knowledge-check; new-doc-verb depends on scaffold-init, so docs/README.md and its index format are fixed before this skill is built, and the done test runs in a repo set up with `kmctl init`.

plugin/skills/write-docs/evals/iteration-1-benchmark.md is an empty aggregate (model "<model-name>", "3 runs each", 0% pass rate, 0 tokens) that contradicts results.md's 4/4 with and without the skill; a reviewer reading it sees a skill that failed every run.

The scripted checks that produced iteration 1's 4/4 (type folder, index entry, kmctl check, no stray page) live only in a session scratchpad grade.py; evals.json holds prompts and prose expected_output but no expectations, so the grading cannot be rerun from what is kept beside the skill.

entries.change: Removed the benchmark skill-creator wrote without grading data; results.md holds the real scores.
Each prompt now lists its expectations, the scripted checks plus the judged type fit and, for the tutorial, no guessed install command.
The grading script is kept beside the skill, takes the iteration folder as its argument and finds kmctl on PATH or KMCTL_BIN.
Names evals.json's expectations and grade.py as the source of the 4/4 scores.

findings.claim: iteration-1-benchmark.md showed placeholder zeros that contradicted results.md
the scripted checks behind 4/4 were not kept

grade.py maps run folders to type folders by hard-coded eval names (tutorial-getting-started, howto-supersede, ...) that evals.json never records, so a fresh skill-creator run with other folder names stops with a KeyError
